guideTitle: 6 Best Motion Sensor Night Lights Under $15 in 2026
metaTitle: Best Motion Sensor Night Lights Under $15 (2026)
metaDescription: Six motion sensor night lights at a very low price point, compared by brightness steps, sensing and power type so a small budget still lights the way.
introParagraphs: At the lowest end of the market, a motion sensor night light has to do one job and do it without fuss: come on when you walk past in the dark, and go away when you leave. The six lights below all clear that bar, and they split into two groups. Four are plug-in units with no batteries, the LOHAS, DORESshop, Lyridz and BriVIVI. Two are battery-free in a different sense, the GOODEA pair that charges by cable and clings to a magnet.

We evaluated each pick on how much control you get for a small outlay. The Lyridz dims from 1 to 50 lumens, the MAZ-TEK steps through 4, 8 and 15 lumens, the LOHAS offers 30 or 60 lumens, and the BriVIVI has an adjustable slide. Where a listing gives no sensing range, we say so rather than guess. We deliberately skipped dusk-to-dawn only lights that have no motion sensor, because they glow all night.

Cheap does not mean careless. A very low price usually costs you pack size, polish or a published sensing range, and the guide explains which of those trade-offs matter in your home. Prices are not quoted here because they change often.

products.name: Lyridz Plug-In Dimmable Motion Night Light
products.description:
The Lyridz stands out in this budget group because it behaves like a more expensive light. Its brightness runs from 1 to 50 lumens, so you can set it nearly dark for a bedroom or raise it for a hallway. A PIR sensor covers 120 degrees out to 13 feet, which is a published figure, something not every budget light provides.

It offers two separate modes. In motion mode, it lights when you walk by in the dark, and in light-sensor mode it acts like a dusk-to-dawn lamp that stays on all night. That flexibility means one product can serve as a hallway motion light in one place and a steady glow in another. The glow is warm and gentle, and the light plugs in with no batteries to replace.

The trade-offs are modest. Thirteen feet is shorter than the longer reaches advertised by some rivals, and the dimming controls take a few minutes to learn. It is sold as a single light, so extra rooms mean extra units. Compared with the LOHAS, which has two fixed levels, the Lyridz is the more adjustable choice, and for a small outlay that adjustability is the main reason to pick it first.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants adjustable brightness without paying for features they will not use.
cons: Dimming takes a minute to learn

products.name: L LOHAS LED Plug-In Motion Sensor Night Light
products.description:
The LOHAS is the light for people who want two obvious choices and nothing else. A slide switch picks 30 or 60 lumens, and a second switch chooses On, Off or Auto. That is the whole interface, and it is hard to get wrong. The 3000K soft white tone suits a bedroom and does not feel clinical.

The On mode turns it into a steady night light, handy at the end of a corridor where you want a constant glow, while Off lets you silence it without pulling it from the wall. Auto uses the built-in sensor to light the room on movement. At 60 lumens it throws plenty of light for a hall, and at 30 lumens it is comfortable beside a bed.

The listing publishes no sensing range, so you will want to place it close to where you walk and see how it behaves. It is sold singly, and its two brightness levels are less flexible than the Lyridz's dimming or the DORESshop's three steps. Choose it when simplicity matters more than adjustability, and for a spare light in a guest room it is hard to fault.
products.bestFor: Households that want the fewest possible settings.

products.name: MAZ-TEK Plug-In Dimmable Motion Night Light, 3 Levels
products.description:
The MAZ-TEK is the dimmest light here, and that is deliberate. Its three levels are 4, 8 and 15 lumens, which is far gentler than the 30 and 60 lumens of the LOHAS. For someone who is easily woken by light, or who wants a glow just bright enough to see a doorway, those low steps are the point.

Three modes keep it simple. In AUTO the light stays off in a bright room and comes on when movement is sensed in the dark, ON holds it constant and OFF turns it off. Four LEDs draw at most 0.5 watts, so it costs very little to run. The warm white tone is easy on the eyes.

The weak side of low output is that it will not light a large room, and 15 lumens is the ceiling, so a long hall may call for a brighter light such as the LOHAS at 60 lumens. The listing does not give a clear sensing range in the excerpt we reviewed. Think of it as a bedroom or bathroom light first, a bedside option that will not blind you at night.
products.bestFor: Light sleepers who want a very low glow.
pros: Three gentle steps from 4 to 15 lumens
cons: No clear range in the listing

products.name: DORESshop Plug-In Motion Sensor Night Light, 3000K
products.description:
The DORESshop is the pick if the light will be seen, such as in a guest bathroom or an entry. Its distinctive shape is intended to double as a decorative accent, which sets it apart from the flat white rectangles around it. It combines motion and light sensing so it only comes on in the dark.

Brightness has three levels, giving finer control than a two-step light like the LOHAS, and the listing quotes a detection range of 2 to 5 meters. The 3000K warm tone keeps a room restful, and the plug-in design means no charging. Setup is simply pushing it into an outlet and choosing a level.

Style comes with a trade-off, since a decorative shape focuses less on raw output and needs an outlet where it can sit comfortably. If your goal is the most light per unit, the LOHAS at 60 lumens is more practical, and if it is the most adjustment, the Lyridz wins. This one is for looks, with function that is perfectly adequate.
products.bestFor: Guest rooms and entries where appearance counts.

products.name: BriVIVI Plug-In Motion Sensor Night Light
products.description:
The BriVIVI is the lowest-friction way into motion lighting in this group. It plugs in, needs no battery and has a switch on the bottom that adjusts brightness. Three modes, AUTO, ON and Off, let it work as a motion light, a constant glow or an off lamp that stays in the wall.

Its sensor reacts to movement from humans or animals in the dark, which means a cat or dog crossing the room can turn it on as well. In a house with pets, that is either a plus, because it lights the pet's path too, or a nuisance, because it triggers more often. The listing does not give a published range in the excerpt.

Because the brightness switch sits on the bottom, it is awkward to change once the light is plugged in, so set it before installing. Compared with the Lyridz, it offers less precise control and no published range, but it is simpler. It makes sense as a spare or a first light, and for the smallest outlay of the six it covers the basics.
products.bestFor: First-time buyers who want the simplest plug-in light.

products.name: GOODEA 2-Pack Magnetic Rechargeable Motion Night Light
products.description:
The GOODEA pair is the odd one out because it needs no outlet. Each light has a built-in rechargeable battery that charges in about two hours, and the listing says it lasts 40 to 80 days with motion triggering. A magnet lets you lift the light off its mount to charge, with no adhesive to scrape.

It senses motion only in the dark, and offers three brightness levels at 25%, 50% and 100% in a warm 3000K tone. Two lights in the pack make it easy to cover a closet and a doorway, or both ends of a short hall. They suit places where an outlet is out of reach, such as inside a wardrobe or beside a cabinet.

The cost of cordless freedom is upkeep, because 40 to 80 days is short for a rechargeable light and you will need to remember to charge it. A metal surface or the supplied plate is needed for the magnet. The listing also gives no confirmed sensing distance. Against the plug-in picks, it is the one to buy only if you cannot use an outlet.
products.bestFor: Closets, cabinets and spots with no nearby outlet.
cons: Requires a metal surface or plate

buyingCriteria.explanation: At a small outlay, brightness control is the best predictor of whether you will still like the light in a month. The MAZ-TEK steps through 4, 8 and 15 lumens, the LOHAS offers 30 or 60, and the Lyridz dims from 1 to 50. A light that is too bright in a bedroom gets unplugged, so aim for the lowest level that shows the floor. A fixed-output light is fine only if the number suits the room.

Cheap lights often hide their range, and that matters when you are deciding where to place them. The Lyridz states 13 feet at 120 degrees and the DORESshop quotes 2 to 5 meters, while the LOHAS and BriVIVI give no figure. A missing range is not a defect, but it means you should plug the light in near your path and walk past it before committing. Sensors respond best to side-to-side movement.

Plug-in units like the LOHAS, Lyridz and BriVIVI have no upkeep at all, but they depend on outlets at floor height. The GOODEA pair runs on a built-in battery that lasts 40 to 80 days, so it goes where outlets do not. The right answer is the one you will not forget. If you will not remember to charge, stay with plug-in.

Warm white is kinder at night than cool white. The LOHAS and DORESshop list 3000K, and the GOODEA lists warm 3000K as well. Cool light can feel harsh at 2 a.m. and may disturb the next sleep cycle. Even at this price, choose a warm tone and a low level.

More modes are only helpful if you use them. The LOHAS and MAZ-TEK give On, Off and Auto, which lets you silence the light for guests or leave it on during a storm. The Lyridz adds a light-sensor mode that works as a steady glow. A plain light with Auto only is fine for a stable routine.

Motion sensors respond to heat and movement, not to people specifically. The BriVIVI listing notes that animals can trigger it, and a wide 120 degree arc like the Lyridz's can catch movement from the next room. Mount the light away from doorways that lead to busy rooms. If you have pets, test it before you fix the position.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control for the money
howWeEvaluated.description: Because every pick sits at the low end, we asked what control each one adds. The Lyridz leads with 1 to 50 lumens of dimming, the MAZ-TEK follows with three gentle steps, and the LOHAS keeps to two levels. Extra control earned credit only when it was practical and clear.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sensing information
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which listings publish a sensing range. The Lyridz gives 13 feet at 120 degrees and the DORESshop gives 2 to 5 meters, while the LOHAS, BriVIVI and GOODEA do not. Published numbers earned more confidence, and missing ones were flagged for a placement test.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared plug-in simplicity against rechargeable freedom. The four plug-ins have no upkeep, while the GOODEA needs a charge every 40 to 80 days. We scored low upkeep higher, but credited the GOODEA where an outlet is impossible.

howWeEvaluated.title: Light quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored warm color and low glare, with the MAZ-TEK at 4 to 15 lumens as the gentlest and the LOHAS at 60 lumens as the brightest. Warm 3000K tones scored well across the group.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The Lyridz leads on adjustability, the LOHAS on simplicity, the MAZ-TEK on low light, the DORESshop on looks, the BriVIVI on entry simplicity and the GOODEA on cordless placement. We avoid quoting prices since they change.

faq.q: Can a very cheap motion night light be any good?
faq.a: Yes, if you accept fewer extras. Plug-in lights such as the LOHAS and MAZ-TEK handle the core job well, and the Lyridz even adds full dimming. What you give up is usually a published range, a larger pack or polish. Decide what you need before shopping.

For a bedroom, 4 to 15 lumens such as the MAZ-TEK is gentle, while a hallway is better at 30 to 60 lumens like the LOHAS. The Lyridz covers both with dimming from 1 to 50 lumens. Start low, because you can always move to a brighter light.

faq.q: Are rechargeable lights worth it at this price?
faq.a: The GOODEA pair is useful where there is no outlet, but its 40 to 80 day run time means recharging a few times a year. If you have outlets, plug-in lights are lower effort. Use the rechargeable pair for closets and cabinets.

faq.q: Why does my light sometimes not come on?
faq.a: Motion lights with a light sensor stay off in a lit room, which is by design. A nearby lamp or streetlight can also keep it dormant. Also check the mode switch, because the Off position will silence it.

faq.q: Will pets set off the light?
faq.a: Often yes. The BriVIVI listing says it reacts to humans or animals, and most PIR sensors respond to any warm moving body. Mount the light higher or at an angle if it triggers too often.

A long-life LED usually outlasts the plug and housing, and plug-in lights have no battery to wear out. Rechargeable lights like the GOODEA depend on battery health. There is no way to guarantee years of use, so choose lights with simple designs.

faq.q: Is there a difference between motion and dusk-to-dawn?
faq.a: Yes. A dusk-to-dawn light stays on all night once it is dark, while a motion light only lights when you move. The Lyridz offers both modes, and the LOHAS gives On for a steady glow. Choose by whether you want constant or occasional light.
